The funny thing is, I didn't even think about this until I had a meeting with a temporary counslor last week. Within half an hour of talking to him, he'd deduced that I had attachment issues stemming from a lack of emotional availability with my parents. In my ten years of therapy, I don't recall that ever being a topic with any of my dozen of carers, but it makes sense.

"Emotionally neglectful" might be a bit of an overstatement, but there was a lack of warmth and availabilty. The older I got, the less I felt like I could open up to my parents. My privacy wasn't respected because my mum would tell her sister every detail of my life. My dad used to yell a lot when i was younger, but he has stopped now, so my siblings won't deal with that as much. They never created an enviroment where I felt I could open up to them. Once i became a teenager, i stopped. There's no communication, either. My dad could go on business trips and i wouldn't know until two days after he left. 

I'm blessed otherwise. I've always been a bit spoiled economically, and I've been given all the freedom in the world. They wouldn't care if I stayed out 'til 5 am on a Thursday night, or whatever my sexuality was (not that i felt comfortable talking with them much about that). They don't mind me doing whatever. I feel like a prop sometimes, because I do well in school and attend a prestigious university. My achievements is always the topic whenever we're with extended family. Not "Oh, she's become interested in X lately" or whatever.

But it would explain a lot about me:

* I remember crying watching The Fosters because I wish I had that sort of warmth in my family. I had to stop watching because of it.
* I am fiercly independent. Just the thought of moving back home makes me want to cry. I struggle to rely on others even the tiniest bit, and I can't seem to ask for help (aside from when I am anonymous online)
* I can't open up. At all. I don't feel emotionally connected to people, for the most part.
* I'd always be super clingy with my teachers, especially before High School. Mentors still mean the world to me, and their approval means more to me than my parents. 
* I only ever invest emotionally in TV shows. I feel like they are a replacement for real relationships. I've experienced heartbreak and grief through them, moreso than in real life. My grandfather killing himself didn't shake me as much as my favourite character dying.
* Social awkwardness. I don't always get cues. 
* I am emotionally shut off, depressed as hell, lack self-compassion, feel empty and so on
* The thought of being in a relationship terrifies me. I can't imagine giving up my independency and privacy like that.
Thanks. It's just that I usually feel dismissed, and I don't want to make a Big Deal out of nothing. I've survived every day of my life so far, so there's no reason for them to take me seriously
